record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.context_brief: Explicit compatible metrics in dimension two
record.original_question: For each gl-regular Nijenhuis operator L in dimension 2, construct explicitly a metric geodesically compatible with L.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.4. For each gl-regular Nijenhuis operator L in dimension 2, construct (explicitly) a geodesically compatible metric.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth 2-dimensional manifold and let $L:TM\to TM$ be a (1,1)-tensor field (a Nijenhuis operator) whose Nijenhuis torsion
$$\mathcal{N}_L(X,Y)=L^2[X,Y]-L[LX,Y]-L[X,LY]+[LX,LY]$$
vanishes identically. Assume $L$ is gl-regular, i.e., at every point $p\in M$ the operator $L_p:T_pM\to T_pM$ has minimal polynomial equal to its characteristic polynomial (equivalently, every eigenvalue has geometric multiplicity one).

A (pseudo-Riemannian) metric $g$ on $M$ is called geodesically compatible with $L$ if the following two conditions hold:
(i) $g(LX,Y)=g(X,LY)$ for all vector fields $X,Y$ (so $L$ is $g$-self-adjoint), and
(ii) the (0,2)-tensor $\nabla^g L$ satisfies $(\nabla^g_X L)Y = \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(d\,\mathrm{tr}(L)\otimes\mathrm{Id} + \mathrm{Id}\otimes d\,\mathrm{tr}(L)\bigr)(X,Y)$ in the standard symmetric form characterising geodesic equivalence; equivalently, the geodesics of $g$, viewed as unparametrised curves, are preserved by the projective connection determined by $L$.

Problem: For every gl-regular Nijenhuis operator $L$ on a 2-dimensional manifold, give an explicit local construction of a metric $g$ geodesically compatible with $L$, expressed in canonical coordinates adapted to the Jordan type (two distinct real eigenvalues, a complex-conjugate pair of eigenvalues, or a single eigenvalue of algebraic multiplicity 2 with a non-trivial Jordan block).
artifact.category_tag: Nijenhuis geometry and geodesically compatible metrics
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work in Nijenhuis geometry (Bolsinov–Konyaev–Matveev, "Applications of Nijenhuis Geometry V") proves that any gl-regular real-analytic Nijenhuis operator locally admits a pseudo-Riemannian metric geodesically compatible with it, with an explicit description via the second companion form, and gives a full description of all such metrics. This yields, in particular, explicit constructions in dimension 2 for the generic gl-regular case, though a uniform explicit treatment covering all Jordan types in dimension 2 is part of ongoing work, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Applications of Nijenhuis Geometry V
status_evidence.snippet: A gl-regular real-analytic Nijenhuis operator L locally admits a pseudo-Riemannian metric g geodesically compatible with L; such g can be given explicitly in terms of the second companion form of L, and all such metrics are described.
status_evidence.claim: Existence and explicit description of geodesically compatible metrics for gl-regular Nijenhuis operators is established, supporting partial resolution of the 2D problem.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis geometry III: gl-regular Nijenhuis operators
status_evidence.snippet: Local normal forms for gl-regular Nijenhuis operators are obtained, providing canonical coordinates in each Jordan type.
status_evidence.claim: Canonical local forms exist that enable explicit metric constructions in dimension 2.
